units: **A milestone without DoD text does not exist.** If you come across one, report it — hanging the issue in it is a guess then.

**Already done?** Ask this before the worktree: an issue that is already done then costs no branch. It is a targeted search on *this* issue, not a bulk scan. Pick a core term from the issue (function, file, config key) and run this as **one Bash call** (not four separate ones; the KPI `leadin` counts every call before the first route call):
**Blocked in a controller run?** (Only if present.) If the line carries `— blocker #  open`:

**Controller run?** (Only if present.) If the prompt ended on `(issue # , controller-run)`, do not call `superpowers:brainstorming` at exit **c**: headless, nobody can answer. Post with `/lighthouse-write-handoff` (controller mode) a handoff with `next: /superpowers:brainstorming` and stop. The controller returns the issue with "needs a brainstorm".

**Links: absolute in chat, relative in files.** In a chat answer a link to a file that exists only on the branch must carry the full absolute worktree path: the IDE resolves chat links against the main checkout. In a `.md` file, relative instead; `.claude/hooks/lighthouse/md-link-check.sh` blocks an absolute path there.
**Only after the worktree.** The agent gets an absolute path; that path must exist.
**The cwd of the persistent shell drifts** back to the main checkout in the middle of a session. Prefix every command with `cd  ` or `git -C  `, otherwise a `sed -i` hits the wrong tree.

**This skill sets exactly two transitions on the board: `To do` and `On hold` → `In progress`.** No labels, no other status. `On hold` is a deliberate parking, and whoever explicitly picks up the issue lifts it. `Controller` (if present) stays: a handover to the controller. For the rest the same line as the board-sweep skill, if present.

**`gh issue list --json` breaks** under the rtk proxy (`Failed to parse gh issue list output`). Use `gh api`. An unknown `--label` filter is moreover silently ignored: you get the full, unfiltered result back and count nonsense.

**b ends at the committed plan.** Plan written and committed → `/lighthouse-write-handoff` (fixed seam). That lets the user choose: plan review, controller (SDD, if present) or interactive (`/superpowers:executing-plans`). Execution follows only after that choice, in a window of its own or through the controller.
2. Read and report the three axes
> The test marker is the contiguous string `not a valid reason`. Do not break it over two lines > when reformatting.

Call `lighthouse-route-issue` with this number. The issue is already in context from step 1, so it makes no new read call. The gates (0–4, first hit wins) and the blocking label as steer live there; it delivers one line:

Copy that line **literally** into your answer, **before** the next `Skill` call. That is what the KPI row `gate` counts (and `scout` the sub-letter); a line that only comes after handing on counts as routed silently.
Delivers `title`, `body`, `labels`, `milestone` and `comments` (the *count*) in one answer. Only if that count is > 0 does a second call follow:

Do not repeat it in the Skill args and do not summarise it; put in the args only the fixed reference `IMPACT PACK: in context, do not repeat`. A summary costs exactly the precision the scout was paid for; a copy pays the same tokens twice. The receiving skill stays responsible itself and reads a source again when a real decision rests on it.

Exception: if the last `🤖 heading:kind_started` on the issue carries the field `stack:` or `blocker:`, the block is already accounted for and you execute the route (`blocker: accounted`: the predecessor is still open, but its PR is merged). An older comment may still carry the old keys `stapel:` or `blokkade:` (`blokkade: verrekend`); they count the same.
From issue number to a read issue, a worktree and one chosen follow-up route. Fills the gap between `/lighthouse-write-issue` (opens the lane) and `/lighthouse-close-issue` (closes it).

Gate `1`, `2` or `4a`: do not execute. Post with `/lighthouse-write-handoff` (controller mode) a handoff `next: /lighthouse-start-issue  ` from the issue's own worktree, and stop. The controller starts it only when the predecessor's PR is green.
Gate `4b` or `4c`: execute the route as always; those already end in a handoff.
Gates `0`, `1`, `2` and `4a` never call it: they have, respectively, a stop, a complete recipe, a debug workflow and an execution that fits in one file.

Gates `4b` and `4c` hand on to a skill that still has to get to know the codebase broadly. That exploration costs main-agent context and repeats between brainstorming, planning and execution. That is why at these two exits — and only at these two — a read-only scout goes first.

If the issue has a milestone, read the `### heading:milestone_dod`, the `### heading:milestone_no_gos` and the `### heading:milestone_not_yet_decided` sections from the milestone description as well. If the issue does not fit according to the first two, say so before you start. If the issue demonstrably touches an open question from the third (a bullet without `→ # `), report one line `fog:  `; in `lighthouse-route-issue` it then falls under c at gate 4. Only a question that demonstrably concerns the work of this issue counts. If the heading is missing or says "None.", no report.
If the line carries `· layer:   ( )` (gate 3) or the reason names an accompanying skill, that travels along as context for the execution.

In scope: the *start* of work on an existing issue in this repo (`forge.repo`) — read it, report the axes, ask whether it is already done, set up the worktree, get the route from `/lighthouse-route-issue` and hand on.
Never `gh issue list --json` — that breaks under the rtk proxy. Always with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`; Go's TLS is blocked otherwise.
New spec/plan files on the project paths instead of the superpowers default folder

Not here: writing or updating an issue (`/lighthouse-write-issue`), closing an issue (`/lighthouse-close-issue`), auditing the state of the board (the board-sweep skill, if present), and executing the chosen route itself — this skill delegates that.

One Agent call, `subagent_type: lighthouse-issue-impact-scout`. In the assignment: the full issue body with the acceptance criteria, the `heading:milestone_dod`, `heading:milestone_no_gos` and `heading:milestone_not_yet_decided` sections of the milestone if there is one, the chosen route (`4b` or `4c`), the absolute worktree path, and the instruction layer plus accompanying skill if gate 3 established them. The agent makes no GitHub call itself.
Only when the input you already have — issue, spec, earlier session context — contains these three concretely:
Pickups at gate 4b/4c with a scout call or a concrete skip reason
Pickups where the skill names the chosen gate explicitly
Report all three, also when they do not change the route. If one is missing, report *that* — then the issue is not right, and that is information in itself.
Report exactly one line, of one of three kinds:
Report the choice in one line: `— stacked on # ` or `— waits for # , handoff posted`.

Report the one `board:` line the script prints. Only `To do` and `On hold` become `In progress`. Without `[forge.board]` (`lighthouse config forge.board.project_number` gives rc 1) the script prints `board: skipped — no [forge.board] configured`. A `board: skipped` line is not a stop: picking up goes on. A `board: ERROR` line (rc 2, broken config) is reported and picking up goes on as well. Skip the step on a `labels.blocked_*` label from step 2: gate 0 stops then, and the board would show `In progress` for work that stands still.
Report the trigger on its own line:
Row 2 sees only `Write`/`Edit`. A file that comes about through a heredoc or `sed -i` does not count — 100% means "of the visible writes".
Row 3 is the bill for the ambient choice. Without that row "a sharp negative boundary" is a claim; with that row it is a number that rises at the next measurement or does not.

Row 5 counts only pickups in which this skill actually loaded; a pickup without the skill is the error rows 1 and 3 measure, not this one. The spread over the gates is a by-catch and shows whether gates 1 and 2 fire at all or are dead wood.
Sessions in which this skill loaded without an issue number in the prompt
Share of pickups where the first visible write fell under `.claude/worktrees/`
Skipping is allowed, skipping silently is not

The "Already done?" call from step 2 raises the lead-in by 1 on purpose: one Bash call, before the first route call. Target ≤ 2 stays, but is reachable only for an issue without comments (read + already done = 2); with comments it is 3.
The `IMPACT PACK` is the answer of the Agent call and is therefore already in the context of the skill (`brainstorming` or `writing-plans`) you call next in this session.
The order *is* the design: the worktree stands before the first write, not after it.

The prefixes come from `lighthouse config labels.location_prefix` and `lighthouse config labels.area_prefix`. Gives one of them rc 1 (not set), report ` : skipped — no labels.  configured` for that axis.
The receiver reads from the line `IMPACT PACK`. If there is thinking before that line, that is a defect in the persona, which forbids such a run-up, and no reason to stop the route.
The scout is an accelerator, not a gate. Brainstorming or planning then does its own exploration.

The status `Controller` (only if present, with a `[controller]` table) stays: the controller selects on it and runs this skill itself. In a controller run `labels.blocked_issue` does not stop at gate 0 and the board stays `Controller`, so there is nothing to skip.
Then update the board, from the worktree and with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`:
This step only reports: it closes nothing and sets no label.
Through `superpowers:using-git-worktrees`, branch `issue- - `. No implementation of your own: that skill chooses between `EnterWorktree` and the `git worktree add` fallback itself.
Timeout, tool error, or output that does not follow the contract:
Tool calls between pickup prompt and first `Skill`/`Write`/`Edit`/`AskUserQuestion`
Unconditional, also at gate 1 and gate 2 below: a spec is a commit, a debug fix is a commit. Exceptions: read-only work, and the user who explicitly says "on main".

Use when starting work on a GitHub issue in this repo — "pick up 610", "start on issue 526", "look at 623". NOTE — for writing an issue, use lighthouse-write-issue; for closing an issue, lighthouse-close-issue; when a number is only mentioned without the intent to pick it up, do not use this skill.

When handing on, name the **project path explicitly**, because it overrules the default of the superpowers skills: specs to `lighthouse config paths.specs`, plans to `lighthouse config paths.plans` — not the superpowers plugin's own folder.
When it fails, the route goes on
`Looks simple`, `context is clear` and every other judgement without those three are **not a valid reason** to skip it.

`already done? likely —  `: stop before step 3 and offer `/lighthouse-close-issue  ` (entry B, which verifies). The user decides. If the user says "carry on anyway", continue with step 3. Controller run (if present): put the choice (close through `/lighthouse-close-issue  `, by the user, or "carry on anyway") as the last text and stop; you never close yourself.

`already done? no — searched for  `: also without a hit, never silence. On to step 3, without a question. Second form, for a mention that does not cover: `already done? no — named in  , does not cover the AC`; that one also goes on to step 3.

`already done? not measurable — fetch failed`: the output contains `FETCH FAILED` and there is no covering hit. The recipe then searched a possibly stale `origin/ `, so zero hits is no `no`. Stop before step 3; the user chooses between trying again and "carry on anyway". Controller run (if present): put that choice as the last text and stop. A covering hit stays `likely`: old data also proves the work was already there.

`git grep` gives exit 1 on zero hits; only exit ≥ 2 (e.g. 128) is an error. Precision goes before recall: only a hit that demonstrably covers the acceptance criteria counts, namely a commit with `(# )` in the subject that delivers the work itself, or code/docs that demonstrably fill in the AC. A mention in a commit body, a spec, plan or "part 1" commit does not count: that is the `no` line below, in its second form.
a label from `[labels]`, at most one
stop, with the reason from the line; no board, no route
the exact files or components touched;
the existing pattern that is followed;
the test path and the verification command.

✅ After b: commit the plan, then `/lighthouse-write-handoff` with the choice review, controller (if present) or interactive · ❌ SDD in the same session, or skip the plan review without a decision of the user
✅ After the worktree `board_start.py` · ❌ overwrite a status other than `To do` or `On hold`
✅ At 4b/4c call the scout or skip it with a concrete reason · ❌ skip it silently
✅ Get the route from `lighthouse-route-issue` and copy its line literally before the next `Skill` call · ❌ route yourself, summarise the line, or name it only after handing on
✅ Leave the pack in context and refer to it with `IMPACT PACK: in context, do not repeat` · ❌ summarise, paraphrase or repeat the pack in the Skill args
✅ Name the project path when handing on · ❌ let superpowers choose its own default folder
✅ Report all three axes · ❌ name only the axis that decided the route
✅ Worktree before the first write · ❌ first change some files and then think of the branch
✅ `gh api …/issues/ ` · ❌ `gh issue list --json` (breaks under the rtk proxy)
